newsitem.title: FRANCE: Legrand says 1996 not best year.
newsitem.headline: Legrand says 1996 not best year.

text.p: Legrand chairman Francois Grappotte said on Friday that he did not expect 1996 to prove to be one of the company's best financial years.
"1996 has not been, at least for the first half, one of the best for Legrand," he told an investment seminar.
"It is no surprise, it is clear the economic climate has not favoured us," he said.
Grappotte stressed, however, that the results trend should be favourable for Legrand in coming years.
"Once we start having more volume, we will see immediate improvements in margins in France and in Italy, which make up one of the group's main markets," he said.
Legrand posted in 1995 a 17.6 percent profit rise to 923 million francs on sales up 6.3 percent to 11 billion francs.
But for the first half of 1996, turnover rose only 1.6 percent on a like-for-like basis.
